newsitem.title: USA: H&R Block cancels CompuServe spinoff vote.
newsitem.headline: H&R Block cancels CompuServe spinoff vote.

text.p: H&R Block Inc said Wednesday it had decided not to present to shareholders at its September 11 annual meeting a proposed spin-off of its interest in CompuServe Corp.

H&R said the decision was based in part on CompuServe's reported first quarter and projected second quarter losses, market uncertainties regarding the online industry, and a September introduction of new interfaces for CompuServe Information Services and WOW! service.

On August 20 CompuServe said it expected a second quarter loss of $0.10 to $0.15 a share, due in part to costs associated with the introduction of CompuServe 3.0 and the release of a new WOW! interface. At the same time, CompuServe reported a first quarter loss of $17.1 million or $0.19 a share, plus non-recurring charges of $17.7 million pre-tax ($12.5 million after tax).

"The (H&R) board continues to believe that a separation of CompuServe is in the best interests of H&R Block shareholders and will continue to consider the matter," Frank Salizzoni, H&R interim president, said in a statement.
